issue.body:
<!-- nexkit:request:maintenance:acceptance-existing-head-health-20260926 -->
<!-- nexkit:pipeline:maintenance -->
## Original request

> Add HEAD /health to the existing Python standard-library label service so clients
> can inspect health response metadata without downloading a response body.
> 
> On the existing loopback listener and CLI-selected port, HEAD /health must return
> HTTP 200 with the same application/json content type and Content-Length value as
> GET /health, and no HTTP response body. GET /health must keep returning the same
> JSON health payload. Preserve the established normalization behavior, unknown GET
> route behavior, CLI startup and deterministic package behavior.
> 
> Add regression coverage using the actual service process and real HTTP requests,
> including a check that distinguishes an empty HEAD response on the wire from a
> client merely hiding a received body. Verify the endpoint from the extracted
> package too. Keep all three configured unit, HTTP and package suites separately
> runnable with useful assertions. Document the endpoint in README.md.
> 
> Keep Python 3.12+ and the standard library. Add no third-party runtime dependency,
> external service or authentication. Do not change NexKit workflows, prompts,
> skills, accepted policy or usage limits. This request does not include a release
> or deployment.
> 
> This is the third and final work item within the owner's previously accepted
> three-item live acceptance scope. Clarify the authoritative specification on the
> GitHub issue and wait for the owner's exact requirement approval before any
> application implementation. Delivery must follow the maintenance pipeline's
> configured human review gate after current checks and independent AI review.
<!-- nexkit:spec -->
Add HEAD /health to the existing Python standard-library label service so clients
can inspect health response metadata without downloading a response body.

On the existing loopback listener and CLI-selected port, HEAD /health must return
HTTP 200 with the same application/json content type and Content-Length value as
GET /health, and no HTTP response body. GET /health must keep returning the same
JSON health payload. Preserve the established normalization behavior, unknown GET
route behavior, CLI startup and deterministic package behavior.

Add regression coverage using the actual service process and real HTTP requests,
including a check that distinguishes an empty HEAD response on the wire from a
client merely hiding a received body. Verify the endpoint from the extracted
package too. Keep all three configured unit, HTTP and package suites separately
runnable with useful assertions. Document the endpoint in README.md.

Keep Python 3.12+ and the standard library. Add no third-party runtime dependency,
external service or authentication. Do not change NexKit workflows, prompts,
skills, accepted policy or usage limits. This request does not include a release
or deployment.

This is the third and final work item within the owner's previously accepted
three-item live acceptance scope. Clarify the authoritative specification on
the GitHub issue and wait for the owner's exact requirement approval before any
application implementation. Delivery must follow the maintenance pipeline's
configured human review gate after current checks and independent AI review.
issue.title: Support HEAD /health metadata requests

acceptance.criterion: HEAD /health returns HTTP 200 with the same application/json content type and Content-Length as GET /health, and sends no response body.
acceptance.evidence: service.py handles HEAD /health by passing the same health payload to respond() with include_body=False. tests/test_http.py compares raw HEAD headers with GET headers and asserts the received wire body is empty; the hosted HTTP suite passed.

acceptance.criterion: GET health payload, normalization behavior, unknown GET route behavior, CLI startup, and loopback listener remain intact.
acceptance.evidence: The existing GET and main() paths are preserved in service.py. The HTTP suite exercises health, normalization, blank and missing text, Unicode, and unknown routes through the real subprocess on a temporary port; the unit and hosted HTTP suites passed.

acceptance.criterion: Regression coverage uses the actual service process and real HTTP requests, and proves the HEAD body is absent on the wire.
acceptance.evidence: tests/http_helpers.py opens a TCP socket, sends a raw HEAD request, reads the response bytes, and returns the bytes after the header separator. tests/test_http.py asserts those bytes equal b"". The hosted HTTP suite passed.

acceptance.criterion: Verify HEAD /health from the extracted package.
acceptance.evidence: tests/test_package.py builds and extracts the package, starts its service process, and checks raw HEAD status, headers, Content-Length, and empty wire body. The hosted package suite passed.

acceptance.criterion: Keep the unit, HTTP, and package suites independently runnable with useful assertions, and document the endpoint.
acceptance.evidence: README.md retains all three separate unittest commands and documents HEAD /health. Current reports show all configured suites passed; I independently reran the six-test unit suite successfully.

acceptance.criterion: Keep Python 3.12+, standard-library runtime, deterministic packaging, and existing controls; do not add a release or deployment.
acceptance.evidence: The local interpreter is Python 3.12.3. The service changes use only existing standard-library modules; scripts/package.py is unchanged; the base-to-candidate diff contains no workflow, policy, dependency, prompt, skill, release, or deployment changes. The hosted package suite passed.

commands: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_unit.py -v — passed, 6 tests
Supplied hosted verification: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_http.py -v — passed, 7 tests
Supplied hosted verification: python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_package.py -v — passed, 6 tests
limitations: The local sandbox disables sockets, so I relied on the supplied hosted verification results for the HTTP and extracted-package TCP checks.

The worktree shows 17 deleted tracked NexKit skill files outside the base-to-candidate commit diff. I left them untouched; the reviewed commit changes only README.md, service.py, and the HTTP/package tests.
